items.title: FPI buying hits 5-year high in November. What's driving the $7.5 billion inflow?
items.description: Foreign portfolio investors returned to the Indian equity scene with a robust investment of $7.5 billion in early November, signaling a shift after a streak of outflows. Key influences on this development included falling crude oil prices and profit-taking related to AI shares. Simultaneously, domestic institutional investors sold stocks amid rising foreign flows, indicating a divergence in market trends.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Nifty closed lower at 25,144 due to rising inflation concerns and higher crude prices. The recent decline follows three consecutive days of gains and reflects profit booking by investors. Although there is marginal consolidation expected, the outlook remains positive with strong corporate earnings. Foreign portfolio investors made significant net purchases, contributing to market support. The rupee fell against the dollar, influenced by weak domestic equities and a stronger greenback.

items.title: Stocks in news: Tata Motors PV, Eicher Motors, Belrise Industries and Patanjali Foods
items.description: Indian equities experienced a decline as elevated domestic inflation impacted investor sentiment and triggered profit booking. The Nifty 50 index fell by 155 points, closing at 25,144. Several companies, including Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Patanjali Foods, reported their quarterly earnings, revealing significant changes in profitability. Notable gains were seen in Eicher Motors and Godrej Industries amidst these varying results.

items.title: Nifty may consolidate before next leg of rally: Analysts
items.description: Nifty is displaying potential exhaustion following a significant rally which may lead to consolidation. Analysts highlight key resistance and support levels which may influence buying opportunities. Recommended strategies include cautious positions and purchasing on dips near critical support zones. Key stocks such as Indus Towers and APL Apollo are also suggested for investment. Observing market movements and strategically planning trades could benefit investors in the coming weeks.

items.title: Stock Radar: Ashok Leyland stock showing signs of recovery after falling by about 20% from highs; what should investors do?
items.description: Ashok Leyland Ltd has recently broken through a key resistance level and its 200-day moving average. The stock experienced a notable fall but found support in the Rs 138-140 zone. Analysts indicate that it may target Rs 210 within the next three to four months. The stock is currently showing strength with increased trading volume and positive technical indicators.

items.title: ET Poll: India growth seen at 7.7% in Q2; on track for 7.3% in FY2
items.description: India’s GDP is estimated to have grown 7.7% in Q2 FY27, supported by resilient consumption, stronger manufacturing and a 22.8% rise in exports, according to an ET poll of 10 economists. Industrial production growth accelerated to 7.3% from 6.2% in the previous quarter, while listed companies reported strong revenue and profit growth.

items.title: Peak repo rate pegged lower at 6%, December hike on
items.description: Most economists expect the terminal, or peak, repo rate at 6%, reversing earlier projections of 6.25%. While some still see the possibility of the policy rate rising to 6.25%, they consider it a low-probability outcome that would depend entirely on incoming data.

items.title: Sun Pharma eyes $4 billion loan for Organon buy, five banks likely to anchor refinancing
items.description: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries is gearing up to secure a substantial $4 billion syndicated loan aimed at refining its financial structure. This initiative is focused on refinancing a portion of the bridge financing used for its acquisition of Organon & Co. The company has recruited five lead arrangers to finalize the loan's terms.

items.title: RBI pushes back on easing microfinance FOIR, flags rising rates and debt risks
items.description: The RBI has rejected calls to relax the 50% fixed-obligation-to-income (FOIR) limit for microfinance borrowers, warning that excluding certain loans from the calculation could understate household debt. Deputy governor Shirish Chandra Murmu said the limit should be treated as a maximum, not a lending target.

items.title: MV Electrosystems shares rally 8% after bagging Rs 325 crore order from Chittaranjan Locomotive works
items.description: MV Electrosystems shares surged on Monday after the company secured a Rs 325.26 crore order from Chittaranjan Locomotive Works for supplying IGBT-based propulsion equipment for electric locomotives. The contract includes three years of maintenance, with deliveries scheduled between April 2027 and January 2028, boosting order book visibility.

items.title: Can Paytm shares finally rise above IPO price? Jefferies hikes target price, estimates after RBI's nod for wallet comeback
items.description: Paytm shares received a boost after the RBI granted preliminary approval for its wallet business to resume operations. Jefferies raised its target price to Rs 2,300 from Rs 2,150, citing monetisation opportunities and improving profitability. The brokerage expects the wallet business to add 3% to FY29 profit estimates.

items.title: Technical picks:  ABB India among 5 stocks to buy this week for healthy returns
items.description: Markets witnessed volatile yet positive trading during the truncated previous week, extending their winning streak to three consecutive weeks. Sentiment remained constructive for most of the week, although profit booking on Friday trimmed the gains. With the Q2 FY27 earnings season entering its final leg, investors will increasingly focus on macroeconomic developments and global cues. Movements in crude oil, the dollar, US Treasury yields and FII flows will remain important determinants of market direction.Here are 5 stock recommendations to buy for healthy returns in short term:

items.title: India Inc profit jumps by ₹1.1 lakh crore in Q2. Is this the start of a virtuous cycle?
items.description: Around 400 major Indian companies reported combined profits of Rs 4.53 lakh crore in Q2 FY27, up from Rs 3.44 lakh crore a year ago, adding nearly Rs 1.1 lakh crore to their earnings. This marks a sharp acceleration compared with the Rs 40,000–50,000 crore profit additions seen in each of the previous seven quarters.

items.title: Vikram Solar shares fall 9% as Q2 net profit plunges 95% to Rs 6 crore; revenue declines 3%
items.description: Vikram Solar shares plunged nearly 9% after Q2 FY27 net profit dropped 95% year-on-year and revenue declined 3%. Lower sales volumes and monsoon-related project delays hurt performance. The company highlighted improving order quality and outlined plans for solar cell and battery storage expansion to strengthen long-term growth prospects.

items.title: Pricol shares crash 20%, selloff wipes out Rs 1,790 crore from market value. What went wrong?
items.description: Pricol shares plunged on Monday after Warburg Pincus agreed to acquire a 38.5% stake in its digital dashboards and instrument clusters business for Rs 1,663 crore. The deal will lead to the demerger of a business contributing 60% of Pricol's revenue, triggering concerns over the restructuring.

items.title: VA Tech Wabag shares tumble up to 11% after Saudi Arabia cancels Rs 2,332 crore desalination project
items.description: VA Tech Wabag shares plunged 11% after the Saudi Water Authority cancelled a Rs 2,332-crore desalination project in Yanbu, for which the company had received a Letter of Award in July 2025. The company is approaching the authority to understand the reasons and next steps. The development comes amid strong Q2FY27 earnings and a sizeable order book.

items.title: Market winners: 16 bluechip stocks beat Nifty 50 with up to 21% gains in a month; is it too late to buy?
items.description: Recently, 16 bluechip stocks have shown remarkable performance, exceeding the Nifty 50 index by gaining as much as 21%. Mahindra & Mahindra and Tech Mahindra led the way with substantial returns. However, experts advise caution as such impressive rallies can prompt market corrections. The influence of foreign institutional investors is significant, and analysts recommend adopting selective investment strategies rather than simply chasing rising prices.

items.title: Nifty profit growth hits 17-quarter high at 27%, upgrades now outpace downgrades. Is earnings cycle turning?
items.description: Nifty50 companies posted 27% year-on-year profit growth in Q2 FY27, the fastest in 17 quarters, beating brokerage estimates. Analyst upgrades also outnumbered downgrades, while banking, metals, oil and gas, and automobiles drove most incremental earnings growth. Motilal Oswal has raised its FY27 and FY28 Nifty earnings estimates.

items.title: Belrise Industries shares jump 11% as Q2 profit rises 25% YoY; revenue grows 17%
items.description: Belrise Industries shares rose sharply on Monday after the auto component maker reported a 25% year-on-year rise in Q2 FY27 profit and 17% revenue growth. The company also secured new orders across commercial vehicles, two-wheelers and three-wheelers, while expanding its manufacturing capabilities and entering CNC fixture supplies.

items.title: Saw the rally coming? How India's mutual funds raised stakes in 11 Nifty stocks before rebound to gain big
items.description: Domestic mutual funds strategically raised their stakes in multiple Nifty stocks over several quarters, leading up to October. These stocks experienced significant gains after the market's recovery began on October 8. Mutual fund ownership rose while foreign institutional investment declined in many of the same companies. The Nifty rallied considerably in November, benefiting primarily from renewed foreign inflows and improved corporate earnings.

items.title: Inox Wind shares tumble 10% as Q2 margins disappoint, CEO resigns. Why Motilal Oswal cut target price, earnings estimates
items.description: Inox Wind shares plunged nearly 10% after disappointing Q2 FY27 earnings, lower growth guidance and CEO Sanjeev Agarwal’s resignation. Net profit declined 36% year-on-year, while EBITDA fell 22%. Motilal Oswal retained its Buy rating but cut its target price to Rs 74, citing execution and profitability concerns.

items.title: Kaynes Technology share price crashes 15% after Q2 shocker. Here’s what spooked investors
items.description: Kaynes Technology share price: Kaynes Technology shares fell sharply on Monday after the company reported a Q2 earnings miss, a sharp rise in debt and material restatements of earlier financial statements. Weak smart-metering performance, negative operating cash flow and an auditor's qualified conclusion over its associate investment have added to investor concerns.

items.title: Jefferies issues strongest Adani call yet, screams buy on 6 stocks and predicts 23% earnings CAGR
items.description: Jefferies has turned bullish on the Adani Group, assigning Buy ratings to all six companies under its coverage and forecasting 23% earnings CAGR through FY29. The brokerage expects a $51 billion capital expenditure programme, improving leverage and stronger cash flows to drive growth. It also flagged elevated debt at some entities and potential contagion risks from inter-group linkages.

items.title: Why is market rising today? Sensex jumps 700 pts, Nifty above 25,300 as D-Street’s rally resumes. 6 factors driving gains
items.description: On Monday, the Indian stock market saw a positive start after the previous Friday's winning streak was interrupted. Both Sensex and Nifty climbed in morning trades, buoyed by robust corporate earnings. However, indices such as Nifty Smallcap 250 and Nifty Midcap 100 faced declines. The market's positive momentum was fueled by Foreign Institutional Investors, but profit booking by Domestic Institutional Investors might restrict further advances amid ongoing inflation worries.

items.title: Retail investors caught the falling knife with Rs 15,000 crore investment. 5 stock bets are already bouncing back
items.description: Amid market uncertainties, retail investors poured nearly Rs 15,000 crore into eight companies that suffered significant declines. Within a month, five stocks, including BSE and HDFC Bank, showed impressive rebounds. Conversely, others like Hindustan Copper and PFC continued their downward spiral. This mixed performance highlights the challenges faced by investors adopting a buy-the-dip strategy, indicating a tendency for large-cap stocks to provide more stability during turbulent times.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Tuesday
items.description: Indian stock markets ended higher, with Sensex gaining 512 points and Nifty rising 147 points. However, broader markets weakened sharply as selling pressure outweighed advances, reflecting cautious investor sentiment and continued profit booking in midcap and smallcap stocks.

items.title: Sebi sets up panel to review key ICDR provisions covering IPOs, FPOs, QIPs
items.description: Sebi has formed an Ashish Chauhan-led sub-group to review IPO and fundraising regulations under the ICDR framework. The panel will simplify disclosures, rationalise procedures and improve capital market access while safeguarding investor protection and market integrity.

items.title: PNB among 4 stocks hitting 52-week highs; stock rallies up to 24% in a month
items.description: Benchmark Sensex climbed 512 points to settle at 82,104 on Monday. Riding the market rally, four stocks from the BSE 100 index hit fresh 52-week highs, touching their highest price levels in the past 12 months. A 52-week high represents the highest price at which a stock has traded over the last year and may indicate heightened market activity and investor interest.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A diagnostics provider for a 7.05% gain, a large-cap communications stock for an almost 7% upmove
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: BSE’s Bankex becomes first Indian sectoral index futures contract approved for US market
items.description: BSE’s Bankex index futures contract has received approval from the CFTC for sale in the United States. This approval allows US investors to access India's banking sector through a regulated platform. The BANKEX index tracks top banking stocks listed on BSE, facilitating exposure or hedging in the market. Increased participation from US investors may enhance liquidity in the derivatives market.

items.title: Weekly Top Picks: These stocks scored 10 on 10 on Stock Reports Plus
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, undertakes detailed company analysis for 4,000+ listed stocks. In addition to detailed company analyses, the report also collates analysts’ forecasts and trend analysis for each component. An average score in Stock Reports Plus is calculated by undertaking quantitative analysis of five key investment tools – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum.

items.title: Sebi sets up sub-group under PMAC to review key IPO norms; NSE's Chauhan to head panel
items.description: Sebi has established a sub-group within its Primary Market Advisory Committee aimed at reassessing regulations related to IPOs and fundraising. The initiative seeks to streamline compliance requirements to foster easier access to capital markets. Key focal points include promoter capital lock-in terms, pricing strategies, and due diligence obligations. The group will evaluate relevant Sebi circulars for potential modifications, with final recommendations to be presented to the PMAC for review.

items.title: Retain capital gains tax on equities, economists tell FM Sitharaman ahead of Budget 2027-28
items.description: Economists recently met with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman to discuss the upcoming Union Budget for 2027-28. They recommended keeping the capital gains tax on equities, opposing industry requests for its abolition. Meeting discussions highlighted the economic improvements and private investment growth, emphasizing the importance of fiscal prudence. Additionally, they suggested boosting the MSME and labor-intensive sectors for employment opportunities.

items.title: Indian equities ride global AI trade unwind: Is D-Street back on foreign investors' radar? BNP Paribas answers
items.description: Foreign institutional investors have poured nearly $8 billion into Indian equities in 15 trading sessions, reversing foreign outflows amid global AI stock concerns. BNP Paribas sees largecaps benefiting from renewed overseas buying and supportive domestic investor flows.

items.title: Sebi forms panel to simplify capital-raising rules
items.description: India's markets regulator has established a 10-member panel to review regulations concerning capital raising by companies. The panel, chaired by Ashish Chauhan of NSE, includes executives from various financial institutions. It will assess eligibility criteria, lock-in periods, and rules for securities allocation and allotment. Furthermore, the group will examine disclosure requirements for initial public offerings and follow-on offers. This initiative aims to simplify regulations and enhance access to capital markets.

items.title: India's investments in US Treasuries jump USD 38.4 bn in Jun-Aug amid FCNR flows
items.description: India's investment in US Treasury securities increased by USD 38.4 billion due to FCNR(B) deposits during three months. The Reserve Bank of India introduced a special facility to encourage these foreign currency deposits. This facility led to significant inflows, improving India's foreign exchange reserves substantially. Experts suggest that investment in US Treasuries may slow down due to the closure of the FCNR(B) window. India's reserves grew to USD 740.

items.title: Jefferies reaffirms 'Buy' on MCX, raises target to Rs 4,300; here's what's driving optimism
items.description: Jefferies has reaffirmed its Buy rating on MCX and raised its target price to Rs 4,300, citing structural growth in options trading, rising investor participation, product expansion and strong earnings prospects despite moderating commodity market volatility.

items.title: Market wrap:  Max Healthcare, Tata Consumer, Tata Motors PV, Tata Steel top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Monday
items.description: Sensex and Nifty ended higher on Monday, with the benchmarks gaining up to 0.63% in a recovery rally. However, broader markets remained under pressure, with midcap and smallcap indices declining. Max Healthcare and Tata Consumer led Nifty gainers, while Tata Motors PV and Tata Steel topped the losers' list.

items.title: Sebi may propose raising FPI beneficial ownership threshold to 25%; plans consultation paper
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is contemplating raising the beneficial ownership stake for foreign portfolio investors from 10 percent to 25 percent. This proposed change aims to simplify compliance and bring India in line with global standards. A consultation paper will be released shortly to collect input from stakeholders on easing regulations.

items.title: Auto sector stocks: Time to look at them without bias? 9 auto stocks from different segments with upside potential of 4% to 23%
items.description: Auto companies were supposed to struggle in the shift to EVs. Most have not, handling the transition better than expected, and moving into new areas while doing so. That is a strength. So, with the market turning, will a sector that has already proved itself attract attention once again? Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, is a comprehensive report that evaluates five key components of 4,000+ listed stocks – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum – to generate standardised scores. The simple average of the above-mentioned five component ratings is normally distributed to reach an average score.

items.title: Swiggy among 10 midcap stocks that dropped up to 50% in CY26
items.description: While the Nifty 50 has declined nearly 4% so far in calendar year 2026, the Nifty Midcap 150 has managed to stay resilient, gaining around 2%. However, the broader midcap index's positive performance masks significant pain beneath the surface. Several constituents have witnessed sharp corrections, with their stock prices plunging 30-50% so far this year. We look at the 10 biggest laggards in the Nifty Midcap 150 that have suffered sharp declines. (Data Source: ACE Equity)
